name: Wildflower Flats
headline: Wildflower Flats is a planned 60-unit, all-affordable, three-story apartment building for adults 55 and older (30-60% AMI) at 1501 2nd Street in Fort Lupton's Vincent Village. It is sponsored by McDermott Properties and won 2026 Round One federal 9% and state housing tax credits.
why_it_matters: It won on its second try. After losing in 2025 Round One, McDermott made the project deeper and more efficient: three more units, a shift of units from 60% to 50% AMI (now 47 of 60 at or below 50%), NGBS Silver, and more federal credit requested. It also uses a Fort Lupton Housing Authority special limited partnership for a property tax exemption, a model already used next door. Those are useful lessons for small-town senior 9% applications.

status.label: Credits awarded; city site plan under review; construction not started
status.detail: CHFA announced the award on 2026-05-21, and its award report as of 2026-09-30 still lists it. On 2026-10-20 the City of Fort Lupton listed the Wildflower Flats Site Plan (SPR26-001) as under review, with the Planning Commission date to be determined. The application targeted closing and construction start for December 2026. There is no public record of a closing or building permit.

next_step: Watch for the Fort Lupton Planning Commission hearing on site plan SPR26-001, then a building permit and the financial closing targeted for December 2026.

key_numbers.meaning: Units are at 30% (7), 40% (6), 50% (34) and 60% (13) AMI, in 2 studios, 42 one-bedrooms and 16 two-bedrooms.

background.text: First try: in 2025 Round One, McDermott applied for a 57-unit version (41 one-bedroom and 16 two-bedroom units; 8 at 30%, 5 at 40%, 22 at 50% and 22 at 60% AMI) and asked for $1,509,564 federal and $650,000 state credit. Wildflower Flats does not appear on CHFA's 2025 Round One award report.

Redesign for 2026: the applicant added three units (including two studios) and four parking spaces. It moved units from 60% to 50% AMI so that 47 of 60 units are at 30-50% AMI, citing a market study finding 45% more income-eligible seniors at 50% AMI than at 60%. It also upgraded from NGBS Bronze to Silver.
Credit request grew over the cycle: $1,580,000 federal at the December 2025 LOI, then $1,780,000 at application and award. State credit was $500,000 throughout.

Local deal: there is no city loan or land contribution in the public record. Local support is a property tax exemption through a special limited partnership with the Fort Lupton Housing Authority, plus support letters from the mayor and the Housing Authority. The applicant also asked for CHFA's discretionary DDA basis boost, citing deep targeting and lower Weld County rents.

Precedent next door: the Housing Authority was also the special limited partner for Sagebrush Apartments (72 units, 1365 2nd Street, opened 2024), helping it get a PILOT tax arrangement. That appears to be the 72-unit family LIHTC in Vincent Village that the application says was completed in October 2023 (match inferred from address and unit count).

Local approvals: McDermott held three concept-plan review meetings with the City, the latest in November 2025 (a concept plan review was completed in May 2024). It said it would submit the site plan before CHFA's decision. The City now lists site plan SPR26-001 as under review.
Community input: a virtual public hearing on 2026-01-15 drew no opposition. Some residents raised concerns that the property would be tax-exempt, and McDermott says it met with them.

Design reuse: Brinkman Construction estimated costs. The application says Brinkman built virtually the same building for McDermott twice before, at Lynwood Senior Apartments in Denver (2022/2023) and at Oakridge.

CHFA calls this the first housing tax credit development for older adults in Fort Lupton. Eaton Senior Communities will provide on-site wellness services, and a grocery store, pharmacy, clinic and recreation center are within half a mile.
